analysis.file_name: GS Pasi - GS raises DC spending estimates thru '28 ... see good visibility into growth 6 Nov 2026.pdf
analysis.title: GS raises DC spending estimates thru '28 ... see good visibility into growth
key_insights: GIR raised US data center construction spending forecasts for 2026/27 to $80bn/$100bn from $67bn/$87bn previously, and introduced a 2028 forecast of $125bn.
GS sees good visibility into continued US data center construction spending growth through 2028 from projects already under construction and announced projects viewed as high probability.

At a baseline of ~$3.5bn construction spending per GW, the ~86 GW currently under construction represents ~$300bn in total construction spend, about 6x 2025 US data center construction. Adding high-probability announcements expands the pipeline to ~$900bn.

About 86 GW under construction gives visibility on another year of double-digit construction growth in 2027. Including announced projects Aterio views as high probability but not yet started, GS sees double-digit growth through 2028 even if no new data centers are announced.
Projects already under construction support strong growth through 2027 and underpin just above half of the 2028 spending forecast, with later project starts layering on top.

On current project timelines spending peaks in 2028 but continues into 2030 at levels above 2026. A large pipeline of medium and low probability projects creates potential for growth to extend further.

Midterm election results add risk, but GS sees a potential outcome as extending the duration of the cycle rather than reducing the total addressable market. States where Democrats are likely to further restrict development account for ~45% of planned data center capacity.
GS thought announced project timelines were already aggressive heading into the election, and sees the midterms as potentially smoothing spending and extending the cycle.
risk_factors: Midterm election results could lead to further restrictions on data center development in states holding ~45% of planned capacity.
Announced project timelines were already aggressive heading into the election.
Significant uncertainty around project probability, with a very large pipeline of medium and low probability projects.
geopolitical: US midterm election results and possible restrictions on data center development in states where Democrats are likely to tighten rules, covering ~45% of planned capacity
